question: Should ClickClack adopt persisted emoji reactions as a durable core message interaction across its API, realtime model, and web client?
rationale: The implementation is broad but coherent and has real-app proof; automation cannot decide whether this new product surface belongs in the core messaging contract.

options.title: Accept reactions as core
options.body: Approve the durable reaction contract, require the TypeScript merge gate to pass, and land this implementation.

options.title: Defer the interaction
options.body: Keep the core message model unchanged and close or redirect the proposal only after maintainers choose a different product boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept reactions as core
recommendation.body: Approve the durable reaction contract, require the TypeScript merge gate to pass, and land this implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: No current-main history owner was available in the supplied review context; this requires the responsible ClickClack product/code owner.
